statement: A monthly tenancy without a formal lease is not covered by Section 9 of the Act.
supporting_quote: A monthly tenancy without a formal lease is not covered by Section 9 of the Act.

statement: A lease agreement cannot be sublet to a different legal entity without the prior written permission of the lessor.
supporting_quote: Clause (f) of the Lease Agreement compels the defendant lessee “not to sublet or give on commission or part with possession of the demised premises or any part thereof without the prior written permission of the Lessor.”

statement: In an Agreement to Sell which provides for specific performance and/or damages, the party who is ready to fulfill his obligation in terms of the contract has the right to elect one of the remedies namely, specific performance or damages when the Agreement to Sell is breached and that the party who is in violation of the Agreement to Sell has no right to elect between the remedies.
supporting_quote: Having considered the above matters and the legal literature, I further hold that the party to an Agreement to Sell who is willing to fulfill his obligation in terms of the agreement is entitled to demand specific performance of the agreement by the violating party when the agreement provides for specific performance and/or damages and the violating party cannot elect the option of forcing the party who has not violated the agreement to accept damages in lieu of specific performance.

statement: Formal admissions recorded at the trial need no further proof unless the Court wants them to be proved.
supporting_quote: According to section 58 of the Evidence Ordinance such formal admissions recorded at the trial need no further proof unless the Court wants them to be proved.

statement: A deed of transfer for valuable consideration cannot be interpreted as a deed of gift due to a statement made by the Notary Public in his attestation.
supporting_quote: If the same wisdom is applied here to the case at hand, owing to the reasons mentioned before, the argument that the deed is a deed of gift owing to the aforesaid statement of the Notary which is not even a condition or term in the main part of the deed must fail.

statement: A right of way of necessity cannot be granted if there is another though less convenient path along which access can be had to the public road.
supporting_quote: A right of way of necessity cannot be granted if there is another though less convenient path along which access can be had to the public road.

statement: A plea of prescription cannot arise without the act or acts of nuisance being admitted.
supporting_quote: The plea is, therefore, not only in law, but also at the stage it was so done, both bad in law, but also contradictory in itself.

statement: Objections as to procedure which were not raised before the trial Court, but were acquiesced in, cannot be raised for the first time in appeal so as to frustrate the entire proceedings.
supporting_quote: Finally, objections as to procedure which were not raised before the trial Court, but were acquiesced in, cannot be raised for the first time in appeal so as to frustrate the entire proceedings.

statement: A person who possesses an immovable property with leave and licence of the owner cannot claim prescriptive title against the owner or his heirs on the basis of the period he possessed the property.
supporting_quote: When a person starts possessing an immovable property with leave and licence of the owner, the presumption is that he continues to possess the immovable property on the permission originally granted and such a person or his agents or heirs cannot claim prescriptive title against the owner or his heirs on the basis of the period he possessed the property.

statement: A usufructuary mortgagee is entitled to compensation for improvements made on the mortgaged property.
supporting_quote: The defendant is entitled to compensation for the improvements in a sum of Rs. 75,000.

statement: The institution of an action ipso facto does not interrupt prescription but only suspends it.
supporting_quote: The argument of learned counsel for the plaintiff that Unambuwe v. Janohamy is wrongly decided cannot be accepted. The institution of an action ipso facto does not interrupt prescription but only suspends it.

statement: A right of servitude of light and air cannot be acquired by prescription by mere enjoyment.
supporting_quote: that a right of servitude of light and air cannot be acquired by prescription by mere enjoyment. i.e., by the mere fact that neighbor has not built on his land for any length of time.

statement: A party cannot make a different case before the Supreme Court than the one they presented in the District Court.
supporting_quote: Explanation 2 The case enunciated must reasonably accord with the party's pleading, i.e., plaint or answer, as the case may be.

statement: A person who enters into occupation of property as a licensee cannot acquire prescriptive right to the property unless they produce an event or overt act that manifests their intention to occupy the property as the owner.
supporting_quote: A person, who is let into occupation of property as a tenant, or as a licensee, must be deemed to continue to occupy on the footing on which he was admitted, until by some overt act by which he manifests his intention of occupying it in another capacity.

statement: A new issue can be framed at a trial on the evidence led at the trial although facts relating to the new issue do not arise on the pleadings.
supporting_quote: Considering all the above matters, I hold that new issues can be framed at a trial on the evidence led at the trial although facts relating to the new issues do not arise on the pleadings.

statement: A person cannot acquire prescriptive title to a property if they possess it as a licensee or agent of the owner, unless they commit an overt act that demonstrates they are possessing the property adverse to or independent of the owner.
supporting_quote: It is a well-established principle of law that, so long as a person possesses a property as the licensee or agent of the owner, that person cannot acquire prescriptive title to that property. Instead, the running of prescription can commence only upon the licensee or agent committing some “overt act” which demonstrates that he has cast aside his subordinate character and is now possessing the property adverse to or independent of the owner of the property and without acknowledging any right of the owner of the property.

statement: The court may draw a presumption of ouster when a party's long and continuous possession of land is not disturbed for a period of 10 years, and the party has not claimed any improvements or plantations on the land.
supporting_quote: The presumption of ouster is drawn in certain circumstances when exclusive possession has been so long continued that it is not reasonable to call upon the party who relies on it to adduce evidence that at a specific point of time in the distant past there was in fact a denial of the rights of the other co-owners.

statement: A decision of a District Judge confirming a final scheme of partition is not an order as envisaged by Section 36A of the Partition Law, if it finally disposes of the matter in dispute.
supporting_quote: In other words, if the District Judge concluded the other way, granting that the alternative scheme of partition was correct instead of granting that the final scheme of partition was correct, then again the matter comes to a finality.

statement: The doctrine of exceptio rei venditae et traditiae cannot be applied when the transfer is of a share that may be allotted by a partition case, if the transferors are not parties to the case.
supporting_quote: The above doctrine cannot be applied to the transfer in deed No.933 (P2) because Sirisena and Welliya have, by the said deed, transferred the share that may be allotted to them by partition case No.7445/P. But they are not parties to the said case.

statement: A person who gets a contingent right to a property subject to a final decree steps into the room and in place of a party to the Partition action and therefore, such a person can invoke section 53(1) to obtain possession of rights that his predecessor got from a final decree of a partition action.
supporting_quote: any person who gets the contingent right to a property subject to the final decree steps into the room and in place of a party to the Partition action and therefore, such a person can invoke section 53(1) to obtain possession of rights that his predecessor got from a final decree of a partition action.

statement: A transferee must hold property for the benefit of the owner or their legal representative if it cannot be reasonably inferred that the owner intended to dispose of the beneficial interest.
supporting_quote: Where the owner of property transfers or bequeaths it, and it cannot reasonably be inferred consistently with the attendant circumstances that he intended to dispose of the beneficial interest therein, the transferee or legatee must hold such property for the benefit of the owner or his legal representative.

statement: A personal action does not necessarily abate with the death of the plaintiff if the stage of litis contestatio has been reached.
supporting_quote: The maxim ‘personalis moritur cum persona’ cannot be uniformly applied to each and every action which qualifies as personal in nature and whether or not the maxim applies must be determined on the fact and circumstances of the instant case.

statement: The possession of a property by a defendant is considered 'undisturbed and uninterrupted possession' if they have been in continuous possession for more than ten years.
supporting_quote: In the presence of the above evidence, it is not difficult to hold that the possession of this property by Defendant is ‘undisturbed and uninterrupted possession’ within the meaning of Section 3 of the Prescription Ordinance.

statement: An appeal abates only against the deceased respondent, but not against the surviving respondents.
supporting_quote: On the death of a respondent, an appeal abates only against the deceased, but not against the other surviving respondents;

statement: Time cannot run against remaindermen in terms of section 3 of the Ordinance.
supporting_quote: As explained above, time cannot run against remaindermen in terms of section 3 of the Ordinance.
